question_text: Define angular momentum. For a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis, derive L = Iω.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The definition
lines: The angular momentum of a particle
about an axis is the moment of its

lines.text: L = r × p,  magnitude L = mvr

steps.why: The particle definition is the seed; the rigid body is a sum of particles.
common_mistakes: Starting from L = Iω itself — that is the thing to be derived.

recall.must_convey: That angular momentum of a particle is r cross p with magnitude mvr.

steps.label: The derivation
lines: For a rigid body, every particle moves
on a circle with the SAME ω, and
v = rω for each. Summing over all

lines.text: L = Σ m v r = Σ m (rω) r = (Σ m r²) ω

steps.why: Two facts do everything: the shared ω (that is what "rigid" means) and v = rω from earlier in this unit.
common_mistakes: Treating ω as different for different particles — rigidity is what lets it come out of the sum.

recall.must_convey: That summing mvr with v = rω gives (Σmr²)ω.
accept: v equals r omega for each
omega comes out of the sum

steps.label: The result
lines: But Σmr² is the moment of inertia I, so
steps.why: The same compression that turned Σmv into p = mv turns Σmvr into Iω.
common_mistakes: Failing to name Σmr² as I, leaving the sum unfinished.

recall.must_convey: That the sum is I, so L = Iω.
accept: sigma m r squared is I
